content.title: Iowa women's basketball survives First Round March Madness scare vs. FDU
content.text: Updated March 21, 2026, 6:16 p.m. CTThe second-seeded Iowa Hawkeyes (27-6, 15-3 Big Ten) open up women's March Madness with a nerve-racking 58-48 win from the friendly confines of Carver-Hawkeye Arena against No. 15 seed Fairleigh Dickinson (30-5, 18-0 NEC).While the old adage of "win and survive" certainly applies here, there were countless points in the game where the Hawkeyes could have faltered against a Knights squad that shot an astonishing 10 3-pointers and held the Iowa offense in check for the majority of the game.At the end, it was Ava Heiden's dominance in the post that helped seal the deal for the Hawkeyes, by finishing with a game-high and a new career-high 29-point performance on 11-for-16 from the floor and 7-for-7 from the free-throw line. Hannah Stuelke also stepped up with a double-double on 13 points and 16 rebounds.Despite the First Round scare, Iowa will advance to the NCAA Tournament's Round of 32 on Monday, March 23, where it will face No. 10 seed Virginia (21-11, 11-7 ACC) from another sold-out Carver-Hawkeye Arena. Survive and Advance Final: Iowa: 58, Fairleigh Dickinson: 48IN HEAVEN, THERE IS NO BEER!!!HAWKEYES WIN!EXHALE, IOWA FANS!Iowa will advance to the Round of 32 to clash with No. 10 seed Virginia on Monday. 3:45 4th Quarter: Iowa: 52, Fairleigh Dickinson: 46FDU Timeout.Ava Heiden is starting to put her mark on this game with 10 straight points, forcing the Knights to call a timeout.All eight of Iowa's points since the Hawkeyes' last timeout have come from the 6-foot-4 sophomore center. 6:16 4th Quarter: Iowa: 44, Fairleigh Dickinson: 43Iowa Timeout.FDU closes the gap again to just one point by going on a 7-0 scoring run fueled by careless Iowa turnovers.The sell-out crowd at Carver-Hawkeye Arena is nervous. End of 3rd Quarter: Iowa: 35, Fairleigh Dickinson: 33Iowa is playing poorly at the end of the third quarter, allowing FDU to remain in striking distance entering the fourth quarter.Iowa needs to wake up offensively in the final 10 minutes or else FDU could pull off an unbelievable upset. 2:37 3rd Quarter: Iowa: 35, Fairleigh Dickinson: 31Iowa Timeout.Iowa cannot buy a basket right now, as FDU's 3-pointer cuts the lead down to just four points. 4:56 3rd Quarter: Iowa: 35, Fairleigh Dickinson: 26Media Timeout.Both teams have simmered down offensively as neither has scored in 2:23 of game time. 7:19 3rd Quarter: Iowa: 35, Fairleigh Dickinson: 26FDU Timeout.Iowa returns to feeding Heiden the ball in the post, where she is nearly automatic, to expand its lead to nine points. Halftime: Iowa: 27, Fairleigh Dickinson: 26Iowa enters halftime with just a one-point lead, as Iowa ran into a scoring drought in the second quarter, and FDU is heading into the break on a 23-9 scoring run.While Iowa opened the game scorching hot from the field, FDU's defensive adjustments have significantly slowed the Hawkeyes offense since. The Knights also have been exceptional from 3-point land, shooting 6-for-16, which equates to 66.6% of their total made buckets from the floor so far.As for Iowa, the Hawkeyes are shooting 12-for-27 from the field, but are an ice-cold 1-for-9 from deep. Ava Heiden leads the team in scoring with 10 points of 5-for7 shooting, with Steulke coming in at second with eight points, followed by Wright's five.As cliché as it may sound, Iowa needs to return to what has carried them all season in the second half: superior post play. While defending the 3-point line better is another must-have adjustment, the key to victory is "controlling the controllables". 4:31 2nd Quarter: Iowa: 26, Fairleigh Dickinson: 21Media Timeout.Iowa responds to FDU's torrid scoring run with one of its own, forcing the Knights into a "one-and-done" style of offense.Iowa will need to continue to follow its game plan, as FDU has proven it can compete with the Hawkeyes by shooting red-hot from the 3-point line. Kate Martin and Lucy Olsen energizing the crowd End of 1st Quarter: Iowa: 20, Fairleigh Dickinson: 17Despite a dominant opening five minutes of this game by Iowa, FDU has stormed back with four 3-pointers to close the quarter down by just three points via a 12-0 scoring run. Lucy Olsen Back At Carver 5:00 1st Quarter: Iowa: 16, Fairleigh Dickinson: 3Media Timeout.Hawkeyes are absolutely relentless offensively and defensively so far, which has the Knights frustrated early and desperately searching for answers. 7:00 1st Quarter: Iowa: 12, Fairleigh Dickinson: 3FDU Timeout.Knights have absolutely no answer for Ava Heiden to start this game, who has six points so far, along with Chit-Chat Wright's five. Iowa’s potential Round of 32 foe set, Hawkeyes’ tipoff delayedAs a result of No. 10 seed Virginia defeating No. 7 seed Georgia in overtime in today's first game, the matchup between Iowa and Fairleigh Dickinson at Carver-Hawkeye Arena will now be delayed past the original start time of 3 p.m. CT.The anticipated start time for the Hawkeyes' game against the Knights is set for around 3:27 p.m. CT.The winner between Iowa and Fairleigh Dickinson will now face Virginia in the Round of 32 on Sunday. No surprises on Iowa's pregame injury reportThere are no surprises on Iowa's pregame injury report. Emely Rodriguez remains out for the Hawkeyes.Where to watch Iowa women's basketball vs. Fairleigh DickinsonWatch Iowa vs. Fairleigh DickinsonTV: ESPNTipoff time: 3 p.m. CTIowa women's basketball opens the NCAA Tournament against Fairleigh Dickinson. Matt Schumaker and Ros Gold-Onwude have the call from Carver on ESPN.Live stream: FuboHawkeye fans can stream Iowa women's basketball vs. Fairleigh Dickinson via Fubo, which offers a free trial to first-time subscribers.Jan Jensen is a Naismith National Coach of the Year semifinalistJan Jensen guides Iowa into the second NCAA Tournament under her watch. Iowa advanced to the round of 32 last season, topping Murray State, 92-57, before falling to third-seeded host Oklahoma.In her second season at the helm, Jensen led Iowa to 24 regular-season wins, which is the second-most for the Hawkeyes over the last 26 years. Iowa also won 15 Big Ten games, the most by a coach in their second season at Iowa.For her efforts, Jensen was recently named a Naismith Women's College Coach of the Year semifinalist.Contact/Follow us @HawkeyesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Iowa news, notes, and opinions.
